title: Interruptible generation garbage collection and client resume protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Partial token generations may accumulate when clients disconnect mid-stream (network failures, client crashes, or long-poll timeouts). Left unmanaged these partials consume memory and KV cache slots and complicate function/tool-call atomicity. This ticket designs and implements a low-latency GC and resume protocol that: 1) ensures quick reclamation of resources from abandoned generations, 2) preserves ability for well-behaved clients to resume recent partial outputs without re-generation, and 3) maintains strong invariants for structured outputs and tool/function calling so downstream side-effects are not duplicated.
acceptance_criteria: Partial generations older than configurable TTL are evicted and reclaimed without leaking GPU memory or KV cache slots
Clients that disconnect and reconnect within resume_window (default 60s) can resume with a resume token and receive exactly-once semantics for function/tool calls (idempotency enforced)
No client-visible increase in 99th percentile tail latency for steady-state streaming workloads (<5% regression on canary) after rollout
Automated chaos tests show >95% success rate for resume scenarios under transient network partitions
Dashboards show eviction count, resume success rate, average reclaimed bytes, and number of blocked batches attributable to orphaned generations
non_goals: Full cross-region resume for private deployments (out of scope for this ticket)
Guaranteeing resume across major model updates that change tokenizer/kv-format
Rearchitecting long-term cold-storage for historical partial outputs (will be a follow-up)
design_decisions: Lease-based ownership: each in-flight generation is owned by a short-lived lease (default 45s) renewed by active clients; leases stored in runtime metadata with epoch IDs
Soft-delete + TTL: on lease expiry mark generation as soft-deleted and start an eviction grace window (default 15s) during which resume tokens are honored; after grace window perform hard GC
Resume tokens are opaque signed strings (HMAC) that encode generation id, epoch, and sanitized KV-prefix pointer. This avoids exposing internal IDs while enabling resume validation
Function/tool-call idempotency: runtime will attach an at-most-once token to each outbound tool call; on resume attempts we validate token ledger to prevent duplicate side-effects

Memory vs correctness trade-off: we will keep minimal prefix caches for resume (configurable max bytes per-customer). If budgets are exceeded we fall back to full re-generation with clear retry headers to clients
SDK changes: add resume() helper methods for JS/Python SDKs that transparently attempt resume when reconnecting and surface structured errors for non-resumable cases
implementation_tasks: Runtime: implement lease metadata and expiry scan job (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287)
Runtime: add soft-delete state and eviction worker with configurable grace window
Runtime: expose resume token generation and verification endpoints; add HMAC key rotation hooks
Runtime: integrate at-most-once ledger for external tool/function calls (small KV table with sliding retention)
API: extend streaming handshake with 'resume_token' optional field in initial resume request
SDK: JS and Python helpers to persist resume token and attempt transparent resume; update error classes
Console: add dashboard tiles for orphaned_generations, resume_success_rate, eviction_latency
E2E: add chaos-monkey test that kills client mid-stream and attempts resume; integrate into CI nightly
Docs: PRD -> Confluence design doc and SDK usage examples
qa_checks: Unit tests for lease expiry and soft-delete transitions
Integration tests against staging runtime simulating 300 concurrent streams with randomized disconnects
Property test to ensure idempotency ledger prevents duplicate function calls even when resume attempts repeat
Load test measuring 99th percentile tail latency before/after change on canary cluster
Manual verification: runthrough with an app that issues tool calls during generation (reranker + external webhook) to validate no duplicate webhooks
rollout_plan: Deploy to staging; run full E2E + chaos suite; validate dashboards
Canary: enable for 5% of traffic for 48h; watch resume_success_rate and eviction_latency
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days contingent on no regressions
Post-rollout: keep flag for 14 days as kill-switch; schedule follow-up to tighten defaults based on metrics
monitoring_playbook: Alert: orphaned_generations_rate > baseline + 5 sigma -> page oncall-runtime
Alert: resume_success_rate < 90% for 10m -> notify runtime and SDK owners
Runbook step: if orphaned_generations spike, trigger immediate short GC iteration and evaluate recent lease renewals; correlate with deployment events
Runbook step: on suspected duplicate tool-call reports, query at-most-once ledger using generation id and reconcile with external service logs
Mitigation: flip feature-flag to disable soft-delete/resume codepath and fall back to existing conservative GC implementation
risks: Resume token leakage could allow denial-of-service or unintended resume if tokens compromised (mitigation: short TTL, HMAC, rotation)
Idempotency ledger growth if we keep entries too long; could increase KV costs (mitigation: windowed retention and compaction job)
Edge cases where resumed generation depends on non-deterministic external tools causing divergent outputs; resolved by preventing resume for non-deterministic tool calls and surfacing clear errors
SDK adoption lag: older SDKs won't know how to resume; we will maintain backward compatibility but lose resume benefits for those clients
